title: Daily Board

letters.name: Safety
letters.sources: Safety Cross, 5S Audit, or by hand
letters.red: An accident or a first-aid case that day.
letters.amber: A near miss, an unsafe condition, or a 5S audit below its target.
letters.green: A day without an incident, once the Safety Cross is in use.

letters.name: Quality
letters.sources: Damage Control, Incomplete Control, Night Audit Log, Room Inspection
letters.red: Damage, incomplete orders or audit exceptions above the target rate. Without a volume: a count clearly above the usual day. Room Inspection: a first-time pass rate below 75 %.
letters.amber: Within 20 % of the target, or above the usual count. Room Inspection: a first-time pass rate below its pass mark.
letters.green: Nothing logged, or a rate under the target. Room Inspection: a first-time pass rate at or above its pass mark.

letters.name: Delivery
letters.red: On-time routes below the target, or more than 60 minutes of breakdown downtime in the Maintenance Planner.
letters.amber: Within 5 points of the target. With only some routes logged, late routes above the usual. A breakdown logged in the Maintenance Planner.
letters.green: On time at or above the target.

letters.name: Cost
letters.red: What you decide, for example overtime above the daily target or unplanned agency staff.
letters.amber: Overtime or extra cost that stayed inside the target but needs a word.

letters.name: People
letters.red: Absences above the target, or a shift that ran short-staffed.
letters.amber: An absence covered, a new starter, a training gap.
letters.green: Everyone there, everyone trained for the work.

safetyMessages: Two hands for the last metres: carry, never throw.
A pallet truck stops at every aisle end. A person is faster than you think.
Wet floor: clean it or sign it before you walk on.
Report the near miss today. Tomorrow it is an accident.
Heavy low, light high, nothing over the edge.
Look up before you lift: beams, sprinklers, cables.
A door that stays open in the rain is a wet floor in ten minutes.
Secure the load before the doors close, not after.
Gloves on for broken glass, torn metal and cold rooms.
If the equipment is damaged, take it out of use. Today, not after the shift.
Walk, do not run. The three seconds you save are not worth a fall.
The new starter does not know the shortcuts are dangerous. Tell them.
tips: The huddle is read, not typed. Open the board, go through the five letters, close with the actions.
Red is a question, not a blame.
A red day asks what happened and who owns the next step. It never asks whose fault it was.
A red without an action is a lie.
Every red day gets an action with an owner and a date in the Action Tracker, or the board decorates the wall.
Let the logs do the work.

Safety, Quality and Delivery fill themselves from Damage Control, Incomplete Control, Delay Analyzer, the Safety Cross, Room Inspection and the Maintenance Planner in this browser. Type only Cost and People.

Quality takes the first-time pass rate of the day from Room Inspection: green at or above its pass mark, amber below it, red below 75 %. The board sets that line itself, because an inspection does not record whether a failed room was given to a guest. Delivery takes the breakdowns of the Maintenance Planner: amber for a breakdown, red for more than 60 minutes of downtime in a day. Overdue tasks on A assets are read out with the actions.
The workplace profile holds the site, the shifts, the areas with their owners and the targets. Every tool reads them.
